haiku-low.q1: A person runs the failover command after deciding it is a real regional loss. Automatic detection only pages on-call; nothing else happens automatically.
haiku-low.q2: The command stops and reports the loss estimate. It continues only with an accept-data-loss override, which is recorded with its approver.
haiku-low.q3: Before promotion: A fenced and the post-fence gate passed or overridden. Before workers start: reconcile complete. Before DNS moves: B's health checks pass.
haiku-low.q4: Sessions are not replicated between regions, so users arrive on B with empty sessions and must sign in again.
haiku-low.q5: Its database is wiped and rebuilt as a replica of B from a fresh base backup, never reused as primary. Failback is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: A's fencer stops Postgres 25 s after its last acknowledged renewal, or sooner on a fence request. The store refuses A's old-epoch renewals.
haiku-low.q7: The lease store. The failover command writes active_region; A's fencer writes lease renewals and reads fence requests; the command reads it on each run.
haiku-low.q8: Reconcile runs first: ledger-done jobs marked done; running jobs with a key requeued with attempt plus 1; running jobs without a key set needs_review.
haiku-low.q9: Re-run the command; it resumes at the last finished step. Going back to A after promotion is not a supported step, and A is never unfenced.
haiku-low.q10: Requests to A fail while A is fenced, and sessions reset on B. The 60 s TTL is sometimes ignored, so DNS propagation takes about 1 to 3 minutes.
haiku-low.q11: Commits after B's replayed position are lost, bounded by the RPO gate at 30 s; steady lag is typically under 5 s. Lost rows are not listed.

sonnet.q1: A person (on-call) runs one failover command after deciding it is a real regional loss. Detection alone only pages on-call: 3 probe sites hit A's /healthz every 10 s, and 2 of 3 seeing 3 consecutive failures triggers the page. Nothing else happens automatically, and there is no promotion.
sonnet.q2: The RPO gate checks three loss measures: recorded replay lag, seconds since B last received WAL, and estimated unreplicated commit age. If any is over 30 s, the command stops, reports the loss estimate and changes nothing. It continues only if the operator gives an accept-data-loss override, which is logged to the store with its approver. The gate is re-run after fencing with A's final position. If that re-run fails and there is no override, A stays fenced, nothing is promoted and service stays down.
sonnet.q3: Before B's DB is promoted: the RPO gate passed or an override was given, A is fenced (fencer confirmed Postgres stopped, or A's lease expired plus 5 s, recorded as fenced at epoch n), the post-fence gate passed or was overridden, and the store accepted the compare-and-set recording promoting at epoch n+1. Before B's workers start: db_promoted is recorded and job reconcile has completed. Before DNS moves: B /healthz passes at full size (12 web instances) with every started B worker having polled jobs, and the store has recorded active region B at epoch n+1.
sonnet.q4: Sessions live in a per-region Redis cluster that is not replicated between regions. Users arrive on B with empty sessions and must sign in again. The brief accepts this.
sonnet.q5: A's old database is wiped and rebuilt as a replica of B from a fresh base backup. It is never reused as primary. A's app and workers stay scaled to zero until the replica has caught up. Failback is a separate planned switchover with its own gate, and there is no automatic failback. An open question asks whether to keep the old database to compare lost rows before the wipe.
sonnet.q6: The fencer, a small service on A's database host. It renews A's lease every 10 s (30 s TTL) and reads fence requests on each renewal. If it cannot renew, it stops Postgres 25 s after its last acknowledged renewal, using its own monotonic clock and pg_ctl stop -m immediate, killing the postmaster if that hangs. The store expires the lease 30 s after receipt, so expiry is always later than the stop. The command waits for the stop report or lease expiry plus 5 s before promoting. Postgres does not auto-start as primary, and the store refuses A's renewals at epoch n. Limit: a wedged host with a live postmaster is not covered by the timing, and the plan says to test that case in a game day.
sonnet.q7: The lease store, a 3-voter store with one voter in A, one in B and one at a third site, needing 2 of 3 for a write. Its active_region field is authoritative, and DNS is only a copy of it. The failover command writes start and finish markers, the epoch, the fence request, the fence record, any override, and the active region. A's fencer writes lease renewals with commit position and time, plus its stop report. The command reads it at the start. DNS is written after the store and never writes to it.
sonnet.q8: Step 5 reconciles every unfinished job row before any B worker starts. If the side-effect ledger shows the job done, the row is marked done and not re-run. Otherwise, a row running under an epoch below n+1 with an idempotency key is requeued with attempt plus 1. A row in that state with no key is set to needs_review for a person to decide. Queued rows with no ledger entry run normally. The command prints the IDs, and attempt counts for requeued rows, so on-call can check external systems for repeats.
sonnet.q9: Each step writes start and finish markers to the store. After a crash or stop, on-call fixes the printed cause and re-runs the command. It reads the last finished step and resumes at the next one, re-checking each step's precondition (for example pg_is_in_recovery before pg_promote), and uses the same epoch. A compare-and-set on the last finished step stops two people running it at once. Going back to A: rolling back to A after promotion is not a supported step, and A is never unfenced. Before promotion, if the failover is abandoned after A is fenced, there is no path to restart A, which is an open question. If the store refuses the promoting write, B stays standby and A stays fenced.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED for a specific client's experience. The document says the global DNS TTL is 60 s and some resolvers ignore it. Until DNS moves, it points at A, which is fenced, so users keep getting failures. DNS propagation is estimated at about 1 to 3 min. If the DNS write fails, DNS stays on A and users keep getting failures until a re-run succeeds. Whether a stale-cached client recovers on its own after its cache expires is not explicitly described.
sonnet.q11: Rows committed on A after B's replayed position are lost, including invoices and payments, not only jobs. The command cannot list the lost rows. The target RPO is 30 s. The gate bounds the loss by the unreplicated commit age, computed from A's last acknowledged renewal plus up to 25 s of commits before the fencer stops Postgres. Steady-state lag is under 5 s. The gate is an admission check, not a guarantee, so unreplicated commits can still be lost. An operator override can accept loss beyond 30 s.
